title: r/PlannerAddicts
tagline: People who buy planner supplies monthly and never quite stop.
audience: Planner enthusiasts who decorate spreads weekly and restock stickers, washi and inserts constantly. A genuinely consumable habit.
overview:
A community organised around a hobby that requires ongoing purchase. Members share weekly spreads, compare planner systems and buy sticker kits on a rolling schedule.

For a stationery seller this is close to ideal: the product is consumed, the community is enthusiastic, and new releases are actively anticipated.
discussions:
Weekly spread photos and layout ideas
Planner system comparisons
Sticker kit and washi hauls
Pen and marker recommendations
Functional versus decorative planning debates
loves:
Cohesive sticker kits designed to work together
New release announcements they can plan around
Help with layout and system problems
dislikes:
Self-promotion outside allowed threads
Design copying between sticker makers
Overpriced kits relative to what's in them
rules:
Promotion restricted to designated threads
Design-theft accusations taken seriously
Haul posts should credit the makers
approach: Release in kits rather than singles and announce ahead of time. This community plans its spending as carefully as its weeks — being on their calendar is worth more than being in their feed.
tags: planner, stickers, stationery, washi, journal, organisation

title: r/bulletjournal
tagline: A large, aesthetic-driven community that buys notebooks, pens and stencils.
audience: Bullet journallers, from minimalist to elaborately artistic. They're particular about paper quality and buy notebooks, pens and tools with real deliberation.
overview:
Organised around a specific journalling method, with a strong visual culture. Spreads get shared and admired, and the supply conversations are detailed — ghosting, bleed-through, paper weight.

The audience cares about materials to an unusual degree, which rewards anyone selling genuinely good notebooks or tools.
discussions:
Monthly and weekly spread showcases
Notebook comparisons — paper weight, ghosting, binding
Pen and brush-pen recommendations
Minimalist versus decorative approaches
Habit and mood tracker layouts
loves:
Specific paper specs — gsm, bleed resistance, lay-flat binding
Spread inspiration that's actually reproducible
Tools that solve a genuine journalling annoyance
dislikes:
Self-promotion in the main feed
Notebooks with poor paper sold at premium prices
Gatekeeping about what counts as a real bullet journal
rules:
Promotion limited to designated threads
Credit expected when reproducing someone's layout
Community leans toward the original method's principles
approach: Lead with paper specifications, not aesthetics. This is one of the few audiences that will read gsm and bleed-through details before buying, and stating them plainly is most of the sale.
tags: journal, notebook, bullet journal, planner, stationery, pen

title: r/weddingplanning
tagline: Couples mid-planning, asking constantly where to find things.
audience: Engaged couples deep in planning, with budgets allocated and deadlines fixed. They ask for vendor and supplier recommendations continuously.
overview:
An intensely practical community where people are actively solving a long list of problems on a deadline. Stationery, signage, favours and decor all come up repeatedly as things to source.

The buying intent is among the highest anywhere — these aren't browsers, they're people with a date and a spreadsheet.
discussions:
Vendor recommendations and warnings
Budget breakdowns and where to save
Invitation, signage and stationery sourcing
DIY-versus-buy for decor and favours
Timeline and logistics planning
loves:
Honest cost information from people who've done it
DIY guidance that saves real money
Etsy and small-vendor recommendations, which circulate constantly
dislikes:
Vendors promoting themselves
Judgement about budget choices
Advice that assumes an unlimited budget
rules:
Vendor self-promotion is prohibited
Disclosure required if you work in the industry
Budget-shaming is moderated
approach: Answer the DIY questions generously, disclosing that you're a stationer. Being visibly helpful about how couples can do it themselves is what makes them decide they'd rather pay you.
tags: wedding, invitation, stationery, signage, calligraphy, favours, event

title: #moderncalligraphy
tagline: Lettering is hypnotic to watch, and event clients hire from this feed.
audience: Lettering enthusiasts, aspiring calligraphers, and — importantly — event planners and brides scouting for someone to hire.
overview:
Calligraphy performs unusually well on video because watching ink flow is genuinely satisfying. The tag serves two audiences at once: people who want to learn, and people who want to hire.

That split is useful — you can sell workshops and practice sheets to the first group while booking event work from the second.
discussions:
Writing videos in close-up, often to music
Nib, ink and paper recommendations
Before-and-after practice progress
Event work — place cards, signage, envelopes
Workshop and class announcements
loves:
Slow, close writing shots with good lighting
Practice-progress posts, which are relatable and popular
Event work photographed in situ at the venue
dislikes:
Fake calligraphy passed off as pointed-pen work
Over-fast videos that lose the satisfying quality
Copying another calligrapher's distinctive style wholesale
rules:
Algorithmic relevance applies to tagging
Credit expected when reproducing someone's lettering style or quote
Paid partnerships require disclosure
approach: Film every commission you letter — the video sells the next booking. Post event work tagged to the venue, because that's how planners and future couples find you.
tags: calligraphy, lettering, wedding, signage, stationery, ink, event
